## Kessler-form evaporation of precipitation (`form: kessler`) {#sec-ch06-kessler}

### Summary

Bulk microphysics schemes in the style of Kessler evaporate precipitation at a rate proportional to the amount of
precipitation and to the subsaturation, both in mole fractions. The `kessler` form replaces the diffusion coefficient
of @sec-ch06-evaporation by $k_3 / n$, which makes kintera's concentration-based rate equal to that mole-fraction
law.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** $\mathrm{d}x_v/\mathrm{d}t = k_3\, x_p\, (x_{\mathrm{sat}} - x_v)^+$, @eq-ch06-kessler-rate.

**Data.** $T$ [K], $p$ [Pa], $c$ [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$]; $k_3$ [$\mathrm{s^{-1}}$] per reaction.

**Placement.** Inside the evaporation evaluator.

**Activation.** `form: kessler` with `k3`; default `form: diffusion`.

**Guarantee / limits.** One condensate to one gas, both coefficient 1.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $k_3$, evaporation coefficient [$\mathrm{s^{-1}}$]; $n$, total molar concentration of gas and
condensates [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$]; $x = c/n$, mole fraction [-]; $x_p$, $x_v$, mole fractions of the
precipitation and its vapor.

### Derivation

kintera sets

$$
\begin{aligned}
n &= \frac{p}{\mathcal R T} + \sum_{\mathrm{condensed}\ i} c_i,\\
\kappa &= \frac{k_3}{n}.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch06-kessler-kappa}

@eq-ch06-kessler-kappa is computed in `forward` ({{< code src/kinetics/evaporation.cpp EvaporationImpl::forward >}}).
With $r = \kappa\, c_p\, (c_{\mathrm{sat}} - c_v)^+$ and $c = n x$ this gives

$$
r = \frac{k_3}{n}\, n x_p\, n (x_{\mathrm{sat}} - x_v)^+ = n\, k_3\, x_p\, (x_{\mathrm{sat}} - x_v)^+ ,
$$

and dividing by $n$, which a closed cell of fixed volume conserves for one-to-one evaporation,

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d} x_v}{\mathrm{d} t} = k_3\, x_p\, (x_{\mathrm{sat}} - x_v)^+ .
$$ {#eq-ch06-kessler-rate}

@eq-ch06-kessler-rate is not evaluated by the code: it is the law that the rate of
{{< code src/kinetics/evaporation.cpp EvaporationImpl::forward >}} reproduces, exact under the stated closed-cell
assumption.

### Numerical method

`forward` computes $n$ per cell from $p$, $T$ and the condensed columns selected by the gas mask, and overwrites
$\kappa$ in the Kessler columns with $k_3 / n$. The mass-action factor and the deficit are those of
@sec-ch06-evaporation. Because $n$ depends on the condensate concentrations, the Jacobian of @sec-ch06-jacobian
carries the derivative of $1/n$ through autograd.

The figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

: Code map of Kessler-form evaporation. {#tbl-ch06-kessler-code}

Refused: an unknown `form`; `form: kessler` without `k3`; `k3` not finite or negative; `k3` without
`form: kessler`; any of `diff_c`, `diff_T`, `diff_P`, `vm`, `diameter` with `form: kessler`; a Kessler reaction
with two products; a direct call without `gas_mask`.

: Tests of Kessler-form evaporation. {#tbl-ch06-kessler-tests}

The box test covers sub- and supersaturated states and a state with no precipitation; CPU only.

### Limits

Only one-to-one reactions. The closed-form agreement assumes fixed $T$ and volume.
